questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university having a good reputation and courses that interest me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy. The university will frequently email you on your university account about any useful information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance apart from attending the required orientation meetings.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Finding housing was very difficult. Almost all available leases are 1-year leases - both from property managers and private sublessors, and American students are less likely to go on exchange in the fall, which makes fall-semester-only leases extremely scarce. I was lucky to find a private sublessor off-campus that was willing to do a fall-semester lease, but it was quite far from the university (direct bus routes made this less of a problem though).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be on the lookout early and often. Join as many Facebook groups as you can find and be wary of scammers. Search on the internet for any potential fall-semester only leases, both from property managers and private individuals. Housing is also expensive in Madison - often more expensive than Copenhagen.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I have heard from others that the cheap apartments in downtown Madison can be in a rough state (black mold, things not working). However, living downtown also makes living a lot easier as you are in walking distance of everything you need.
I lived in a house in a privately-owned house in the University Hill Farms area, which was in a very good condition and close to the A-Bus Line which runs every 15 minutes which made getting to the University easy enough. However the busses don't run pass midnight so you have to get an Uber if you're out at night. I was also reliant on others for driving me to go grocery shopping as there were no options in a walkable distance.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was difficult to figure out which courses I was allowed to take.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The university has its own website where you can register for courses when it opens up in April. However you need certain requirements to be able to register for courses, which is why you need to email the professors of the courses you want to take before the course registrations open up.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The course registration process was confusing at first, as I was not aware that I had to email professors to be able to take their courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I only emailed them after it opened up so there were a few courses that I would've liked to have taken that got filled up quick. There were also some Computer Science courses that I would've liked to have taken that were not available for exchange students, and some Computer Science classes also get filled up quickly.
However the university offer so many courses that I did not have a problem finding other courses that I was interested in. I also got permission by the professors to enroll in all the courses I wanted to enroll in.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Find out which courses you want to take early, and email professors before course registration opens up. 
Also be aware that not all courses on their course catalog list will be available for you to take as some of them are only available in specific semesters. Only on the course registration website can you see which ones are available to you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was taking a mix of undergraduate (BA) and graduate (MA) level courses. Classes closer to level 300 might be for early undergraduates but that does not necessarily mean that they will be easier than courses with a higher course number.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
A lot of classes only have 50 minute lectures (no discussion class and no breaks during lecture), which means you're not going to be meeting a lot of people in your classes. The amount of coursework varies from class to class (some had very little while other courses felt like 20 ECTS worth of coursework). 
Overall I found the workload to be very high compared to KU, and at times very overwhelming, especially with weekly assignments and weekly quizzes in multiple courses + midterms and larger projects as well. However, actually passing a course felt less stressful than at KU because your grade is not dependent on the final exam only, but on all the coursework throughout the semester. American students are also going to be a lot more determined to come to class and do well, compared to in Denmark, probably because they paid a lot of money to go to university.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of them except for COMP SCI 300, unless you have good Java skills, as it is a very intensive and time consuming course otherwise.

questions.answer:
Lunch options at the university were a lot more expensive than i expected ($9-$14).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university offers a lot of opportunities, but I often found myself too busy with my coursework to pursue some of them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of sports games happen all the time. Getting student tickets was impossible and very expensive to buy through resellers though.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to an american football game at Camp Randall just for the vibes, even if you don't know anything about the sport. I would also recommend seeing women's volleyball and men's basketball.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of bars downtown and the alcohol is cheap. Otherwise there are a lot of free options in Madison (e.g. Arboretum, Zoo). I would also recommend going to Chicago, Devils Lake, or the beach in Milwaukee when the weather is nice.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. People in Wisconsin are very talkative and hospitable, and it's not significantly different from anything in Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to talk to strangers.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: For a lot of American undergraduates, university is basically their whole life. It seems to be more normal for them to spend all their time on university-related stuff, both academic and non-academic. I was not used to having so much of my time be devoted to the university.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people were so friendly and hospitable.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Find housing early. 
Don't take multiple difficult courses.
Bring warm clothes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look up your courses and professors on sites like ratemyprofessor. It can be extremely important for determining whether or not you should take a course.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting and living with Americans, and experiencing their culture first-hand.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The coursework was often overwhelming.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Try Culver's and get their concrete mixer as well. Possibly the best fast food in the US.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
